claims.claim: A skill is a folder with SKILL.md; an open standard.
claims.evidence: agentskills.io/home: 'a skill is a folder containing a SKILL.md file'; 'originally developed by Anthropic, released as an open standard'. claude.com/docs/skills/overview also calls it an open standard.

claims.claim: About 100 tokens of metadata load at startup, body on activation; only name+description read before activation.
claims.evidence: Spec Progressive disclosure: Metadata (~100 tokens) = name and description loaded at startup; Instructions '< 5000 tokens recommended' loaded on activation. Home page: discovery stage loads 'only the name and description'. Anthropic overview: '~100 tokens per Skill'; body 'Under 5k tokens'.

claims.claim: name 1-64 chars, lowercase/digits/hyphens, no leading/trailing/consecutive hyphens, must match folder.
claims.evidence: Spec name field: 1-64 chars; 'unicode lowercase alphanumeric (a-z, 0-9) and hyphens'; must not start or end with a hyphen; must not contain '--'; 'Must match the parent directory name'. Note: Claude Code makes name optional and defaults it to the folder name.

claims.claim: description up to 1,024 chars; up to 200 for skills uploaded to the Claude app.
claims.evidence: Spec: description 1-1024 chars. Claude Help Center 'Creating custom skills': name '(64 characters maximum)', description '(200 characters maximum)'. Anthropic API/best-practices pages still say 1,024, so 200 is specific to claude.ai upload.

claims.claim: SKILL.md body under 500 lines.
claims.evidence: Spec: 'Keep your main SKILL.md under 500 lines.' Anthropic best practices: 'under 500 lines for optimal performance'. It is a recommendation, not an enforced limit.

claims.claim: Exact list of allowed frontmatter fields and which are required.
claims.evidence: The files show name and description as required (correct) and use license and metadata in examples, but the fields table omits compatibility and allowed-tools. Spec fields: name (req), description (req), license, compatibility (max 500 chars), metadata (string-to-string map), allowed-tools (space-separated, Experimental).
claims.correct_statement: Spec frontmatter has six fields: name and description required; license, compatibility (max 500 chars), metadata, allowed-tools optional. Host extras (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex openai.yaml) are not part of the spec.

claims.claim: Optional scripts/, references/, assets/; evals/ not in spec.
claims.evidence: Spec lists scripts/, references/, assets/ as optional conventions and says any additional files or directories are allowed; evals/ is not named. Nuance: the agentskills.io guide 'Evaluating skill output quality' says 'Store test cases in evals/evals.json inside your skill directory' (fields skill_name, evals[].id, prompt, expected_output, files, assertions).

claims.claim: A rule against XML tags in name/description.
claims.evidence: The open spec has no XML rule. Anthropic docs: name and description 'Cannot contain XML tags'; name 'Cannot contain reserved words: "anthropic", "claude"'. The user's validate_skill.sh and skill_audit.py check neither the XML rule nor reserved words.
claims.correct_statement: No XML tags in name or description, and no 'anthropic' or 'claude' in name, are Anthropic-host rules (Claude API/claude.ai), not Agent Skills spec rules.

claims.claim: Claude API: /v1/skills, container.skills, 20 skills/request, 30 MB, no network or runtime installs.
claims.evidence: Skills guide: 'You can include up to 20 Skills for each request.' 'Total upload size must be under 30 MB (uncompressed)'. Endpoints /v1/skills; container parameter with type (anthropic|custom), skill_id, optional version. Overview: API 'No network access', 'No runtime package installation'. No beta header appears in current examples.

claims.claim: Claude Code: ~/.claude/skills; listing uses 1% of context; full network access.
claims.evidence: Claude Code skills page: personal path ~/.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md; 'The budget scales at 1% of the model's context window' (raise via skillListingBudgetFraction or SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET); each entry capped at 1,536 chars. Overview: Claude Code 'Full network access'.

claims.claim: Codex: .agents/skills; list '<2% of context (or 8,000 chars)'.
claims.evidence: Codex docs: repo $CWD/.agents/skills, user $HOME/.agents/skills, admin /etc/codex/skills. Budget: 'this list uses at most 2% of the model's context window, or 8,000 characters when the context window is unknown'.
claims.correct_statement: Codex skill list uses at most 2% of the context window; 8,000 characters applies only when the window size is unknown.

claims.claim: OpenAI API /v1/skills: 50 MB zip, 500 files per version.
claims.evidence: OpenAI Skills guide: 'Maximum zip upload size is 50 MB.' 'Maximum file count per skill version is 500.' Also 'Maximum uncompressed file size is 25 MB.' Skills attach via tools[].environment.skills; front matter validation follows the Agent Skills spec.

claims.claim: Cursor: .agents/skills or .cursor/skills.
claims.evidence: Cursor docs: project .agents/skills/ and .cursor/skills/; user ~/.agents/skills/ and ~/.cursor/skills/; for compatibility also loads .claude/skills/, .codex/skills/ and their ~ versions.

claims.claim: disable-model-invocation: true locks sensitive operations (which hosts).
claims.evidence: Claude Code: 'Set to true to prevent Claude from automatically loading this skill.' Cursor: 'only included when explicitly invoked via /skill-name'. Codex has no such frontmatter; it uses agents/openai.yaml allow_implicit_invocation (default true). Not in the open spec.
claims.correct_statement: disable-model-invocation is a Claude Code and Cursor field. In Codex set allow_implicit_invocation: false in agents/openai.yaml.

claims.claim: allowed-tools is experimental and not a security boundary.
claims.evidence: Spec: 'Experimental. Support for this field may vary between agent implementations.' Claude Code: allowed-tools 'does not restrict which tools are available: every tool remains callable, and your permission settings still govern'; also 'A skill can grant itself broad tool access'. The phrase 'not a security boundary' is the files' wording, consistent with both.

claims.claim: skills-ref validate <path>.
claims.evidence: Spec Validation section: 'skills-ref validate ./my-skill'. The skills-ref README adds: 'intended for demonstration purposes only' and 'not meant to be used in production'; install is from source (pip install -e . or uv sync).

claims.claim: Write descriptions in third person.
claims.evidence: Anthropic best practices: 'Always write in third person. The description is injected into the system prompt, and inconsistent point-of-view can cause discovery problems.' This is Anthropic guidance, not an open-spec rule.

new_findings.finding: claude.ai and Claude desktop install: Customize > Skills > + > Create skill > Upload a skill > ZIP of the skill folder; toggle each skill on/off; type / in chat to pick one. The Help Center says plans are Free, Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise; claude.com/docs says Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise.
new_findings.source: Claude Help Center: Use skills in Claude; claude.com Skills overview
new_findings.practical_use: Package each skill as a ZIP whose top folder name equals the skill name, keep description at or under 200 characters, then upload at Customize > Skills.

new_findings.finding: Plugins are the bundle-and-share path on claude.ai and Claude desktop: Customize > Plugins > Discover, Add > Add marketplace (Git repo URL or owner/repo), or Add > Upload plugin (.zip or .plugin holding one .claude-plugin/plugin.json). A plugin's skills work in chat, Cowork and Claude Code; plugins installed on the account download to Claude Code on next signed-in session (run /reload-plugins). Team/Enterprise can share a plugin with specific people or publish it to the org.
new_findings.source: claude.com plugins overview; Claude Code plugins overview
new_findings.practical_use: Wrap the whole skill kit as one plugin (.claude-plugin/plugin.json + skills/<name>/SKILL.md) to install once and get it on claude.ai, desktop, Cowork and Claude Code.

new_findings.finding: Org-wide skills: Organization settings > Plugins & skills (Team and Enterprise). Owner-provisioned skills are on by default and users can toggle them off. Group-specific distribution is Enterprise only, via a plugin assigned to a group. Skill scanning of third-party skills is on by default from 2 October 2026 for Enterprise orgs that have not set it.
new_findings.source: Claude Help Center: Provision and manage skills for your organization
new_findings.practical_use: If you ever run a team, an Owner can push a skill to everyone without each person uploading a ZIP.

new_findings.finding: Claude Code syncs your claude.ai skills (download-only) into ~/.claude/skills/synced/ when you sign in with /login using a claude.ai account (v2.1.273 or later). It does not sync with an API key or Bedrock. Edits in synced/ are overwritten; change the skill on claude.ai. Turn off with syncClaudeAiSkills=false.
new_findings.practical_use: Upload once to claude.ai and it also appears in Claude Code; do not edit the synced copy.

The API overview says custom skills do not sync across surfaces, claude.ai skills are individual-only, and claude.ai has no org-wide distribution. new_findings.finding: Claude Code frontmatter is wider and looser than the spec. All fields are optional (description 'recommended'; name defaults to folder name). Extra fields: when_to_use, arguments, argument-hint, disable-model-invocation, user-invocable, disallowed-tools, model, effort, context (fork), agent, background, hooks, paths, shell. Listing entry cap is 1,536 chars for description + when_to_use. `claude plugin validate .claude/skills` checks frontmatter (v2.1.233+). Skills reload live in a session.
new_findings.practical_use: Keep portable skills to spec fields; put Claude Code-only fields in a separate copy or note them as host-specific.

new_findings.finding: Claude API skills: custom skills are workspace-wide; container.skills entries use type anthropic or custom with skill_id and optional version (date-based for Anthropic, skver_ id for custom); no beta header in current examples; also on Claude Platform on AWS and Microsoft Foundry; Agent Skills is not covered by ZDR.
new_findings.practical_use: Pin versions in production calls; keep sensitive data out of skills on ZDR accounts.

new_findings.finding: Codex: $skill-installer for curated skills; 'for reusable distribution of your own skills, prefer plugins'; disable with [[skills.config]] enabled=false in ~/.codex/config.toml; agents/openai.yaml holds allow_implicit_invocation, interface and dependencies; symlinked skill folders are followed; changes detected automatically (restart if not); /skills or $ to mention a skill.
new_findings.practical_use: For Codex, express invocation control in agents/openai.yaml rather than frontmatter.

new_findings.finding: OpenAI API skills attach through tools[].environment.skills on the shell tool; a base64 zip can be inlined instead of creating a hosted skill; limits 50 MB zip, 500 files per version, 25 MB per uncompressed file; front matter follows the Agent Skills spec.
new_findings.practical_use: Keep bundles under 25 MB per file and 500 files to be portable to OpenAI as well as Anthropic.

claims.claim: Do not invent frontmatter fields or host limits
claims.evidence: Spec lists six fields (name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools). skills-ref ALLOWED_FIELDS and Anthropic quick_validate.py both reject other top-level keys. Caveat: Claude Code adds fields, so the rule must be host-aware.

claims.claim: Label facts [SOURCE]/[INFERENCE]/[UNVERIFIED]/[PROPOSED]
claims.evidence: Project convention. No official page read prescribes labels. Not contradicted.

claims.claim: Ask for 3-5 triggering and 3-5 near-miss requests
claims.evidence: Near-misses are strongly supported ('the most valuable negative test cases are near-misses'). The official eval set is about 20 queries, 8-10 each way. The kit itself is inconsistent: 3-5 (master prompt), 10 and 10 (Reference 4.2), 20 at 60/40 (Omnibus).
claims.correct_statement: Use about 20 trigger queries (8-10 should-trigger, 8-10 near-miss should-not); 3-5 is fine only as Phase 0 seeding.

claims.claim: Decide whether a skill is the right mechanism versus memory, tools, hooks or subagent
claims.evidence: No such gate step in the best-practices page, skill-creator SKILL.md or the spec. Reasonable design choice; not contradicted.

claims.claim: At least 3 realistic tasks, baseline without the skill, record the gap, add no instruction that closes no gap
claims.evidence: Best-practices 'Build evaluations first': identify gaps without a Skill, build three scenarios, establish baseline, 'Write minimal instructions'. Checklist: 'At least three evaluations created'. skill-creator: 2-3 test prompts, with-skill and baseline runs spawned in the same turn.

claims.claim: Trigger set with should-trigger and near-miss, separate validation set, test triggering apart from output quality
claims.evidence: agentskills.io: train about 60%, validation about 40%, keep validation results out of revisions; output quality is covered in a separate guide.

claims.claim: One default approach with a short escape hatch, no menus of equal options
claims.evidence: Best-practices 'Avoid offering too many options': provide a default (with escape hatch).

claims.claim: Scope each skill to one coherent job; focused skills outperform sprawling ones
claims.evidence: SkillsBench v1 abstract: 'Focused Skills with 2--3 modules outperform comprehensive documentation'. That concerns module count, not one-job-per-skill.
claims.correct_statement: Evidence supports focused skills (few modules); 'one job per skill' is an extrapolation.

claims.claim: Portable frontmatter fields only; host-specific metadata in host-specific files
claims.evidence: Spec has six fields, not two. Claude Code keeps its extensions in the same SKILL.md frontmatter and ignores unrecognized fields without error, so 'host-specific files' is the kit's own design, not official practice.

claims.claim: Lean SKILL.md, explicit steps, relative forward-slash paths, references one level deep, say when each reference is read
claims.evidence: Best-practices: 'Concise is key', 'Always use forward slashes', 'Keep references one level deep'. Spec: 'Keep file references one level deep from SKILL.md'.

claims.claim: Script rules: non-interactive, --help, explicit inputs, useful errors, distinct exit codes, safe rerun, --dry-run, bounded output, documented dependencies, no hidden network calls
claims.evidence: agentskills.io 'Using scripts': avoiding interactive prompts is 'a hard requirement'; --help; helpful errors; idempotency; dry-run; meaningful exit codes; predictable output size; state prerequisites. 'No hidden network calls' is not stated there.

claims.claim: Do not present experimental host controls as universal security boundaries
claims.evidence: Spec: allowed-tools is 'Experimental. Support for this field may vary between agent implementations'. Claude Code: it pre-approves tools. 'Audit bundled files before installation' is not in the pages read.

claims.claim: Check each host's documentation; limits do not transfer between hosts
claims.evidence: Real differences found: description 1024 (spec/API) vs 200 (claude.ai upload) vs 1,536 listing cap incl. when_to_use (Claude Code); API 20 skills per request, under 30 MB, no network; claude.ai can install packages.

claims.claim: Test battery: structural, with/without, trigger, adversarial/security, regression
claims.evidence: Structural, baseline and trigger tests are official. Adversarial and regression tests are not in the pages read. Official advice missing from the battery: test on Haiku, Sonnet and Opus; repeated trials; human review.
claims.correct_statement: Add a Haiku/Sonnet/Opus matrix and repeated runs to the test phase.

claims.claim: Fix underlying causes, not keywords from failed examples; move repeated helper logic into scripts
claims.evidence: agentskills.io: 'Avoid adding specific keywords from failed queries - that's overfitting'. skill-creator: 'Generalize from the feedback'; 'Look for repeated work across test cases' then put it in scripts/. 'Add corrections to Gotchas' not found.

claims.claim: Final delivery bundle: tree, full files, install steps, results, audit, changelog
claims.evidence: Project convention; no official counterpart found in the pages read.

claims.claim: Collect 10 triggering and 10 non-triggering requests
claims.evidence: Fits 'about 20 queries: 8-10 that should trigger and 8-10 that shouldn't'. In the official flow the assistant drafts the 20 queries and the user reviews them (skill-creator Step 1); the kit asks the user to supply them.

claims.claim: Break the skill on purpose and confirm each test fails
claims.evidence: Not an official step. Closest official checks: skill-creator analyzer flags 'assertions that always pass regardless of skill (non-discriminating)' and 'high-variance evals (possibly flaky)'. Same aim, different method.

claims.claim: Description up to 200 characters for skills uploaded to the Claude app
claims.evidence: Help center: 'Claude uses this to determine when to invoke your skill (200 characters maximum).' Name '64 characters maximum'.

claims.claim: SkillsBench (arXiv 2602.12670, version 1): focused skills with 2-3 modules beat comprehensive documentation; self-generated skills gave no average benefit
claims.evidence: v1 abstract (13 Feb 2026): 86 tasks, 11 domains, 7 agent-model configurations, 7,308 trajectories; curated Skills +16.2 pp average pass rate; 'Self-generated Skills provide no benefit on average'; 'Focused Skills with 2--3 modules outperform comprehensive documentation'. Current abstract page is a later revision with different numbers (see N10).

claims.claim: Freedom calibration: prose for creative loops, scripts for precision
claims.evidence: Anthropic gives three levels: high (text instructions), medium (pseudocode or scripts with parameters), low (specific scripts). The kit's two-way split omits medium.

claims.claim: Lock sensitive operations behind disable-model-invocation: true
claims.evidence: Documented Claude Code field ('Set to true to prevent Claude from automatically loading this skill'). Not in the portable spec; skills-ref ALLOWED_FIELDS and quick_validate.py reject unknown keys (inference, not run), and other hosts ignore it silently. Conflicts with the kit's own step 11 (validate with skills-ref).
claims.correct_statement: It is a Claude Code extension, not a portable lock, and portable validators reject it.

claims.claim: Trigger evals: 20 queries split 60/40
claims.evidence: agentskills.io and skill-creator both: about 20 queries, 8-10 each way, 60% train / 40% validation. Kit omits 3 runs per query, 0.5 trigger-rate threshold, up to 5 iterations, best iteration chosen by validation pass rate. 'Similarity loops' is not an official term.

claims.claim: Double-blind test matrices comparing with-skill against baseline
claims.evidence: With-skill vs baseline is official. Blind comparison is 'optional, requires subagents, and most users won't need it', and means one independent judge not told which output is which. 'Double-blind matrices' is not official wording.
claims.correct_statement: Official: with-skill and baseline runs together; optional blind comparison by an independent agent; mean plus or minus stddev; human review for subjective output.

claims.claim: name 64, description <1,024, body <500 lines
claims.evidence: Spec: description 'Max 1024 characters' (1024 allowed). Body 'under 500 lines' and '< 5000 tokens' are recommendations, not limits. Metadata about 100 tokens is correct.
claims.correct_statement: description at most 1,024 characters; body recommended under 500 lines and about 5,000 tokens.

claims.claim: 20 skills per request, 30 MB uncompressed, no network or runtime installs
claims.evidence: Skills guide: 'You can include up to 20 Skills for each request'; 'Total upload size must be under 30 MB (uncompressed)'. Best-practices: API 'Has no network access and no runtime package installation'.

claims.claim: Frontmatter without XML tokens
claims.evidence: Anthropic: name and description cannot contain XML tags; quick_validate.py rejects '<' and '>' in the description.

claims.claim: Validate structure with skills-ref validate
claims.evidence: Spec 'Validation' section gives 'skills-ref validate ./my-skill'. Caveat: skills-ref README says 'intended for demonstration purposes only' and 'not meant to be used in production'.

claims.claim: Script checks description presence and length
claims.evidence: awk reads only the first line after 'description:'; a folded '>' description becomes length 1 and is never checked, giving a false PASS (matches the local test result).
claims.correct_statement: Official validators parse real YAML (strictyaml in skills-ref, PyYAML safe_load in quick_validate.py); the script should too.

claims.claim: Script validates frontmatter
claims.evidence: Line parser rejects any line without a colon, including valid indented continuations of block scalars, then resets fields to {} so 'name is missing' and 'description is missing' are false follow-on errors. Nested metadata keys are flattened to top level.
claims.correct_statement: Use a real YAML parse; valid folded descriptions must not fail.

claims.claim: Scripts enforce the official frontmatter rules
claims.evidence: Name length, charset, hyphen rules, folder match and 1024 limit exist (subject to the parse bug). Missing: unknown top-level key rejection, compatibility max 500 string, metadata map, angle brackets (quick_validate), reserved words (documented), 200-char claude.ai limit, NFKC normalisation of name/folder.

claims.claim: An unindented second description line is valid YAML as a plain multi-line scalar
